ARCHITECTURE.md §6 "Module contracts" — 1.4.0 hook additions by P2. Each hook is generic; with nothing registered every RUN
path is the 1.3.0 one (proven by the HOOK NO-OP digest: L1-60 × 3 seeds × {passive, idle, strongj} at High and Low).
=========================================================================================================================

§6.2 engine.js
- setInputMode('steer' | 'aim', opts?) — opts { range, k, follow, maxSpeed, keySpeed, dragTop, x } override SQUAD.aim (range
  3.4 m, k 6.8 m per steer.kFraction·W_eff px, follow 18 /s, maxSpeed 14 m/s, keySpeed 12 m/s, dragTop 0.35; x = the lane's
  start). 'aim': the drag / keys / stick move input.aimTargetX, input.aimX follows on the fixed step, targetX stays; a drag
  starts only below dragTop of the screen height (horde CONTROLS: the lower 65 %), while a tap counts anywhere.
  resetSteering() (every level start and quitToTitle) returns to 'steer' with the lane at 0 and scalerGuard to 0 / true.
  Getter inputMode.
- Tap classifier: every non-UI pointer while playing (a second finger included) → input.tap { seq, x, y, t } when released
  within SQUAD.steer.tapMaxMs and never SQUAD.steer.tapMaxPx from its press; pointercancel never taps. 4 pointer slots.
- Action keys: Digit1-4 → input.action 'snap' 0-3, Shift+Digit1-4 → 'repair' 0-3, R → 'repair' −1, gamepad X (button 2) →
  'repair' −1; only while playing, not from form controls; input.action.seq counts them.
- input.activityM: see §3 (sampled in _stepAll).
- pause(data): data rides state:change and is the `pause` payload.
- scalerGuard { exemptMs, dropOk }: each frame's JS minus exemptMs feeds the raise test; dropOk false holds every drop (tier
  and the software-GL render-scale rungs). Defaults 0 / true, restored by resetSteering() at every level start, so a hold that
  ends (won, lost, quit, restarted) can never leave the next RUN level unable to drop a tier. Tier freezes stay
  freezeQuality(seconds).

§6.3 render.js
- setRig('run' | a RENDER.rigs key, s?) — blends the camera to the rig over s seconds of unscaled time (default the rig's
  tween 1.5; 0 snaps), eased inOutCubic: portrait pose / landscape pose by the preset blend; portrait keeps the preset's
  horizontal FOV, landscape uses rig.landscape.hFovDeg with the vertical FOV clamped to fovClamp; the count dolly and the
  framing constraint apply to the follow preset only. The fog moves to rig.fog (far × params.fogFar / WORLD.fog.far: 90 on
  Low / software GL) through env.setFog over s; 'run' restores the current district's fog. level:start snaps the camera back
  to 'run' (the district reset sets the fog); idleCamera(true) (quitToTitle) sets 'run' too, the rig easing out over its
  tween under the title blend (quitToTitle has already applied the district fog). Getter rig. RENDER.rigs.hold: portrait
  camera (0, 10.8, 10.3) looking down z to −11, its pitch derived from wallZ / wallFrac so the ground at z −3.5 (the centre
  line of the 0.8 m deep barricade behind its −3.9 face) projects at 71.5 % of the height on EVERY portrait aspect (the
  preset's FOV differs: 55° at 390×844, 46.3° at 360×640, so one fixed pose cannot hold 69-73 % on both); landscape (0, 9.7,
  15.9) → (0, 0, −12), hFov 50°, vFov 30-50°; fog 58 / 100. Projected (three r170, build/P2/checks/rig.txt): wall 71.5 % and
  face line 69.8-70.1 % at 390×844 / 360×640 / 320×568; 2 m sections 94.8 / 86.8 / 77.2 px; landscape wall 73.9-74.2 %,
  sections 67.7 px (844×390), 58.3 (585×340), 102.1 (1024×594).
  HOLD SCREEN measurement convention (P6 / P7 screenshot rows): measure the wall line AND the 2 m section widths on the
  ground centre line z −3.5 (horde-v2's convention; it reproduces horde-v2's own 92.8 / 85.7 / 76.1 px with the spec pose).
  On the face line z −3.9 the same sections read 75.6 px at 320×568 and 57.4 px at 585×340, under the 76 / 57 px limits,
  although nothing changed: the margins are thin (z −3.5: 77.2 vs 76 px, 58.3 vs 57 px), so a row that measures on another
  line reports a false fail. The spec's own portrait pose (horde §2) puts the wall at 68.78 % at 390×844, which is why the
  rig derives its pitch from wallFrac instead.
- addWarmable(obj) → Promise: obj (under the scene, hidden or not) gets every program of the committed tier compiled
  (_compileChunked restricted to obj, a few per frame) and is drawn once out of sight; it is listed in render.warmables.
  Its out-of-sight draw runs on its own: concurrent addWarmable calls (e.g. Promise.all(crowd.prepare, hold.prepare)) and a
  tier-change / restore warm-up never cancel one another.
  Being in the scene it is part of every later tier change (_prepareTier) and context-restore warm-up. removeWarmable(obj)
  unlists it. Crowd / hold meshes join the scene at their prepare() and are warmed here, so none compile at boot.
- lightsVersion: increments whenever a light colour / intensity / direction changes (district apply / fade frames, title
  swing); consumers with copied light uniforms (crowd) refresh when it changes.
- Icon atlas 512 × 128: RENDER.icons.order in the top cell row, RENDER.icons.row2 (kit, kit2, airstrike, flare, supply) in
  the third (cell = ICON_COUNT + col; the rows between stay transparent against mip bleed); ofItem 'item.kit' / 'item.kit2'.
  iconUV / iconDataURL accept either row; the atlas recipe paints both, so a GPU loss restores row 2 too.

§6.4 models.js
- export tagPart(geo, partId, pivot, hex, emissive?, tag?) and mergeTagged(geos, label) (merges tagPart-ed parts, disposes them).

§6.5 squad.js
- setFormation('run' | 'wall', opts?) — 'wall': SQUAD.formations.wall (21 columns 0.34 m apart over x ±3.4, rows 0.34 m
  behind a front row at world z −2.3, filled row by row centre out; the first 40 slots, the front row and the centre of the
  second, are the shooters); the rows at z ≤ stepBackZ (−1.0) stand opts.stepY / 0.45 m up on the firing step, so their
  muzzles are at 1.40 m. Gameplay (logicalCount, halfWidth, depth, centerZ, shooterPosition, slotWorld, intersectsCircle,
  bounds, the D5 drawn set) reads the wall table at once; records are re-anchored about x 0 (squadX → 0) and ease to their new
  slots over opts.easeS / 1.5 s (smoothstep), the step height with them (the instance matrices draw the step rows at that
  height). The wall ignores input.targetX and the lane lock. reset() returns to 'run'. Getter formation. In 'wall' the count
  label sits at SQUAD.formations.wall.label (0, 0.4, 0): over the rear rows, below the barricade and clear of the screen's
  bottom edge (84.7 % of the height at 390×844, 86.8 % at 844×390). removeSoldiers(n, reason, x, z) defaults z to the front
  row (the wall's z −2.3), so a hold that passes no position loses front-row soldiers first.

§6.6 troops.js
- setPlacement(provider | null) — provider.place(key, out { x, y, z, yaw }) → true moves that troop's slot (out arrives
  holding the formation slot; yaw applies while the troop is not aiming). reset() (every level start, RESTART, QUIT) clears
  it, so a hold sets it at its dig-in and never leaks it into the next RUN level.
- The default slots are RUN slots: the sniper, drone and medic follow the formation (centerZ / slotWorld), but the flamer
  (z = ANIM.flamerFrontOffset = −SQUAD.rowPitch, −0.294) and the APC (z = −(apc.ahead + apc.length / 2) = −5.2) are
  absolute, anchored to the RUN front row at z 0. In 'wall' (front row z −2.3) the flamer would stand inside the rear ranks
  and the APC would straddle the barricade (−3.5 … −6.9), so the hold's placement provider MUST place all five (horde §8:
  sniper and drone as the hold needs, flamer at the wall centre ('4 m' in horde §8), medic unchanged, APC behind the weakest
  section); return false only for a troop whose default slot is wanted.
- With no zombie target, the sniper (highestHp, applyHit with pierce 1; the boss keeps the shot when its HP ≥ the unit's),
  the flamer (nearest + damageInCone) and the drone (nearestOfType('runner') then nearest; its bullets hit providers through
  weapons) use the first live weapons target provider that offers the method. A flamer burning a provider's units opens
  its jet and sways like one burning zombies.

§6.7 zombies.js
- forEachAlive(fn) calls fn(id, type, x, z, hp, yaw).
- spawn() while ctx.hold.active counts ctx.debug.dropped['zombies.spawnInHold'] and warns once (a hold's units are crowd units).

§6.9 gates.js
- liveEvents(out, max) → n: the unpassed (non-decorative) events nearest first as reused rows { id, layout, z, lanes } in
  out[0 … n − 1] (out[0] = activeEvent's event); one row object per event slot. Allocation-free; do not retain the rows.

§6.11 weapons.js
- setPolicy(p | null) (a level start clears it). p.rate(C) → rounds/s (≤ FIRE.spawnRateCap; the fold keeps the RUN weighted
  output: w = max(1, C/weightDiv)·target/rate); p.shot(k, SHOT) aims the k-th logical shooter's round — SHOT arrives as
  { ox, oy, oz = squad.shooterPosition(k), dirX 0, dirZ −1, weight 1, tracerY = p.tracerY or NaN, spread 0, bossOnly false };
  the round's weight is the folded weight × SHOT.weight; tracerY is the tracer's height at the end of its range (cosmetic);
  spread (rad) draws ctx.rngShot; bossOnly rounds test only the boss capsule; returning false fires nothing. Under a policy
  the RUN spread jitter (FIRE.bullet.spreadDeg ± 2°, the minigun's ± 5°) is replaced by SHOT.spread (default 0: no jitter).
  p.weaponFrame(id, FRAME) (FRAME arrives as { x 0, halfWidth 0, z0 = the muzzle front, z1 = WORLD.spawnZ, tx NaN, tz NaN,
  radius 0 }; false = the RUN pattern): rocket → with a target (tx, tz) it flies over the zombies, providers, gates and crates
  (only the boss capsule stops it) and detonates at the target (horde §8: the densest 1 m cell); without one it flies down x
  to z1 and detonates on the first hit; splash radius (0 = data). The rocket's reach stays WEAPONS.rocket.maxRange (30 m
  from the launch point): a target farther than that bursts in the air at 30 m on its line, over whatever is there, so the
  policy searches its densestCell within 30 m of the blob centre (the horde feed band at z −46 … −70 is out of reach).
  railgun → the bolt down x from z0 to z1 (unlimited targets); laser → beams spread across x ± halfWidth from z0 to z1;
  shotgun → only the pellet fan narrows, to ± atan(halfWidth / WEAPONS.shotgun.range) (5.1° for 1.25 m, against the RUN
  ± 10°); the pellets still start at the shooters and fly 14 m, and their x is not clamped. minigun (horde §8 "lane × 3 with
  half-width 1.6 m") → every minigun round that is not bossOnly ends in the lane: a round whose heading (the policy's aim,
  then SHOT.spread) would cross the lane's far end — FRAME.z1, or the end of its 42 m reach (FIRE.bullet speed × life) when
  that is nearer — outside x ± halfWidth is re-aimed from its muzzle at a point of the lane drawn from ctx.rngShot; rounds
  already aimed into the lane keep their heading. The rounds still start at the shooters (z0 is not used), so a flank
  shooter's round converges on the lane over its flight: near the wall it is still beside the lane. The × 3 is the
  minigun's fire config (rateMult 3 with its 0.4 s spin-up, folded by rate(C)); the frame never changes a round's weight or
  count (node checks: framed and unframed minigun DPS are equal). To detect the active weapon, compare weapons.weapon with
  the data ids (WEAPONS.minigun.id = 'weapon.minigun', never the bare key). p.pierce → handed to providers.
- addTarget(provider, priority) / removeTarget(provider); targetCount / targetAt(i). reset() (every level start, RESTART,
  QUIT; weapons resets first in RESET_ORDER) clears the policy AND every provider: register providers at the hold's dig-in
  (or after the level's reset), never once at boot. A provider needs hitTestSeg(seg, radius, out { id, x, y, z, t }) and
  applyHit(id, damage, pierceMax, x, y, z, cause) → leftover (the provider walks its own column: the 1.4.0 "pierce in the
  crowd provider's applyHit"); optional damageInCircle (rocket blasts), damageInLine (rail, laser), nearest / nearestOfType /
  highestHp (+ out.hp) / densestCell / damageInCone (troops, the hold policy); alive === 0 skips it (the sweep, rocket
  blasts, rail / laser lines and the troops). Sweep order: zombies → providers (ascending priority) → boss → gates →
  crates; the smallest t wins, ties go to the earlier one. Squad rounds pass policy.pierce (1 without a policy), drone
  rounds 1.

§6.12 fx.js — listens to fx:burst, fx:decal, crowd:kills (§5).

§6.13 audio.js — AUDIO_CUES[id].on cues, audio:loop, music:mode (§5); MUSIC.modes.hold with MUSIC.instruments.brass (the
  bar chord's root and fifth an octave down, two detuned saws through a low-pass, held a bar; a swell bar: × 1.8, 1.2 s attack).
  loopActive(id) for tests. A loop plays only while the state is 'playing': the pause menu, the brief overlay, the Android
  Back pause and every menu silence it, and it re-plays at once on resume.
